readings.title: Transfer of Terrestrial Authority
readings.subtitle: Yehoshua Commissioned for the Conquest
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 31:1] And Mosheh went and spoke these words to all Yisra’ĕl,
[2] and he said to them, “I am one hundred and twenty years old today. I am no longer able to go out and come in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said to me, <dq>‘You do not pass over this Yardĕn.’</dq>
[3] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> is passing over before you. <dn>He</dn> shall destroy <dn>את</dn> these nations from before you and you possess them. Yehoshua himself is passing over before you, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken.
[4] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall do to them as <dn>He</dn> did to Siḥon and to Oḡ, the sovereigns of the Amorites and their land, when <dn>He</dn> destroyed <dn>את</dn> them.
[5] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give them over to you, and you shall do to them according to all the command which I have commanded <dn>את</dn> you.
[6] “Be strong and courageous, do not fear nor be afraid of them. For it is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> who is going with you. <dn>He</dn> does not fail you nor forsake you.”
[7] And Mosheh called Yehoshua and said to him before the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl, “Be strong and courageous, for you are going with this people to the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn to their fathers to give them, and you are to let them inherit it.
[8] “And it is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who is going before you, <dn>He</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> is with you. <dn>He</dn> does not fail you nor forsake you. Do not fear nor be discouraged.”

readings.title: The Sabbatical Mandate
readings.subtitle: Rehearsing the Torah During the Release
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 31:9] And Mosheh wrote <dn>את</dn> this Torah and gave it to the priests, the sons of Lĕvi, who bore the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and to all the elders of Yisra’ĕl.
[10] And Mosheh commanded them, saying, “At the end of seven years, at the appointed time, the year of release, at the Festival of Sukkot,
[11] when all Yisra’ĕl comes to appear before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the place which <dn>He</dn> chooses, read <dn>את</dn> this Torah before all Yisra’ĕl in their hearing.
[12] “Assemble <dn>את</dn> the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your sojourner who is within your gates, so that they hear, and so that they learn to fear <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and guard to do all the Words of this Torah.
[13] “And their children, who have not known it, should hear and learn to fear <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> as long as you live in the land you are passing over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn to possess.”

readings.title: The Prophecy of the Hidden Face
readings.subtitle: The Divine Song as a Witness
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 31:14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, the days have drawn near for you to die. Call <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Appointment, so that <dn>I</dn> command him.”</dq> And Mosheh and Yehoshua went and presented themselves in the Tent of Appointment.
[15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared at the Tent in a column of a cloud, and the column of a cloud stood above the door of the Tent.
[16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, you are about to sleep with your fathers. And this people shall rise and whore after the mighty ones of the strangers of the land into the midst of which they shall enter, and forsake <dn>Me</dn> and break <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant which <dn>I</dn> have made with them.</dq>
[17] <dq>“Then <dn>My</dn> displeasure shall burn against them in that day, and <dn>I</dn> shall forsake them and hide <dn>My</dn> face from them, and they shall be consumed. And many evils and distresses shall come upon them, and it shall be said in that day, ‘Is it not because our <dn>Elohim</dn> is not in our midst that these evils have come upon us?’</dq>
[18] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall certainly hide <dn>My</dn> face in that day, because of all the evil which they have done, for they shall turn to other mighty ones.</dq>
[19] <dq>“And now write down <dn>את</dn> this song for yourselves, and teach it to <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl. Put it in their mouths, so that this song is to <dn>Me</dn> for a witness against the children of Yisra’ĕl.</dq>
[20] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bring them to the land flowing with milk and honey, of which <dn>I</dn> swore to their fathers, and they shall eat and be satisfied and be fat, then they shall turn to other mighty ones, and they shall serve them, and scorn <dn>Me</dn> and break <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant.</dq>
[21] <dq>“And it shall be, when many evils and distresses come upon them, that this song shall answer before them as a witness. For it is not to be forgotten in the mouths of their seed, for <dn>I</dn> know <dn>את</dn> their thoughts which they are forming today, even before <dn>I</dn> bring them to the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to give them.”</dq>
[22] And Mosheh wrote <dn>את</dn> this song the same day, and taught it to the children of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Covenant Guarantee
readings.subtitle: Placing the Torah Beside the Ark
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 31:23] And <dn>He</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua son of Nun, and said, <dq>“Be strong and courageous, for you are to bring the children of Yisra’ĕl into the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to them, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> am with you.”</dq>
[24] And it came to be, when Mosheh had completed writing <dn>את</dn> the Words of this Torah in a book, until their completion,
[25] that Mosheh commanded <dn>את</dn> the Lĕvites, who bore the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying,
[26] “Take <dn>את</dn> this Book of the Torah, and you shall place it beside the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and it shall be there as a witness against you,
[27] for I myself know <dn>את</dn> your rebellion and <dn>את</dn> your stiff neck. See, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then how much more after my death?
[28] “Assemble unto me <dn>את</dn> all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, so that I speak these words in their hearing and call <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth to witness against them.
[29] “For I know that after my death you shall do very corruptly and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you. And evil shall come to you in the latter days, because you do <dn>את</dn> what is evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to provoke <dn>Him</dn> through the work of your hands.”
[30] So Mosheh spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl <dn>את</dn> the words of this song till their completion:

readings.title: The Perfect Rock
readings.subtitle: The Harmony of YeHoVaH and the Corruption of Men
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:1] “Give ear, O heavens, and let me speak; And hear, O earth, The words of my mouth.
[2] “Let my instruction fall as rain, My speech drop down as dew, As fine rain on the tender plants, And as showers on the grass.
[3] “For <dn>I</dn> proclaim the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Ascribe greatness to our <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[4] “The Rock! <dn>His</dn> work is perfect, For all <dn>His</dn> ways are right-ruling, An <dn>Ěl</dn> of truth and without unrighteousness, Righteous and straight is <dn>He</dn>.
[5] “A twisted and crooked generation has corrupted itself, Their blemish, they are not <dn>His</dn> children.
[6] “Do you do this to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O foolish and unwise people? Is <dn>He</dn> not your Father, who bought you, Who created you and established you?

readings.title: The Allotted Inheritance
readings.subtitle: Establishing Boundaries and Sustaining Ya‘aqoḇ
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:7] “Remember the days of old, Consider the years of many generations. Ask your father and let him show you, Your elders, and let them say to you:
[8] “When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance When <dn>He</dn> separated the sons of Aḏam, <dn>He</dn> set the boundaries of the peoples According to the number of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
[9] “For the portion of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>His</dn> people, Ya‘aqoḇ <dn>His</dn> allotted inheritance.
[10] “<dn>He</dn> found him in a wilderness, And in a wasted, howling desert. <dn>He</dn> encompassed him, <dn>He</dn> made him understand, <dn>He</dn> watched over him as the apple of <dn>His</dn> eye.
[11] “As an eagle stirs up its nest, Flutters over its young, Spreading out its wings, taking them up, Bearing them on its wings.
[12] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> alone led him, And there was no strange mighty one with him.
[13] “<dn>He</dn> made him ride in the heights of the earth, And he ate the fruit of the fields, And <dn>He</dn> made him to draw honey from the rock, And oil from the flinty rock,
[14] "Curds from the cattle, And milk of the flock,With fat of lambs, And rams of the breed of Bashan, And goats, with the choicest wheat; And you drank wine, the blood of the grapes.

readings.title: The Rebellion of Yeshurun
readings.subtitle: Forsaking Eloah for Foreign Entities
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:15] “But Yeshurun grew fat and kicked; You grew fat, you grew thick, You are covered with fat; So he forsook <dn>Eloah</dn> who made him, And scorned the Rock of his deliverance.
[16] “They moved <dn>Him</dn> to jealousy with foreign matters, With abominations they provoked <dn>Him</dn>.
[17] “They slaughtered to demons – not <dn>Eloah</dn> – Mighty ones they did not know, New ones who came lately, Which your fathers did not fear.
[18] “You neglected the Rock who brought you forth, And forgot the <dn>Ěl</dn> who fathered you.

readings.title: The Execution of Justice
readings.subtitle: The Judgment of the Hidden Face
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:19] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw, and despised, Because of the provocation of <dn>His</dn> sons and <dn>His</dn> daughters.
[20] “And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>‘Let <dn>Me</dn> hide <dn>My</dn> face from them, Let <dn>Me</dn> see what their end is, For they are a perverse generation, Children in whom there is no trusting.</dq>
[21] <dq>“They made <dn>Me</dn> jealous by what is not <dn>Ěl</dn>, They provoked <dn>Me</dn> with their worthless matters. But <dn>I</dn> make them jealous by those who are no people, <dn>I</dn> provoke them with a foolish nation.</dq>
[22] <dq>“For a fire was kindled in <dn>My</dn> wrath And burns to the bottom of She’ol, And consumes the earth and its increase, And sets on fire the foundations of mountains.</dq>
[23] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> gather evils upon them, <dn>I</dn> use up <dn>My</dn> arrows upon them –</dq>
[24] <dq>“Wasted by scarcity of food, And consumed by heat and bitter destruction, And the teeth of beasts <dn>I</dn> send upon them, With the poison of serpents of the dust.</dq>
[25] <dq>“The sword bereaves from the outside, And fear from within, Both young man and maiden, Nursing child with the man of grey hairs.</dq>
[26] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> said, ‘<dn>I</dn> should blow them away, <dn>I</dn> should make the remembrance of them To cease from among men,</dq>
[27] <dq>If <dn>I</dn> did not fear the enemy’s taunt, Lest their adversaries misunderstand, Lest they say, “Our hand is high, And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not done all this.” ’</dq>

readings.title: A Nation Void of Counsel
readings.subtitle: The Stored Vengeance of the Rock
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:28] “For they are a nation lost to counsel, And there is no understanding in them.
[29] “If they were wise, They would understand this, They would consider their latter end!
[30] “How would one chase a thousand, And two put ten thousand to flight, Unless their Rock had sold them, And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had given them up?
[31] “For their rock is not like our Rock – Even our enemies are judges.
[32] “Their vine is of the vine of Seḏom And of the fields of Amorah; Their grapes are grapes of gall, Their clusters are bitter.
[33] “Their wine is the poison of serpents, And the fierce venom of cobras.
[34] <dq>Is it not stored up with <dn>Me</dn>, Sealed up among <dn>My</dn> treasures?</dq>
[35] <dq>Vengeance is <dn>Mine</dn>, and repayment, At the time their foot slips; For near is the day of their calamity, And the matters prepared are hastening to them.’</dq>

readings.title: Compassion and Retribution
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Vindicates His Righteous Remnant
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:36] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rightly rules <dn>His</dn> people And has compassion on <dn>His</dn> servants, When <dn>He</dn> sees that their power is gone, And there is no one remaining, Shut up or at large.
[37] “And <dn>He</dn> shall say, <dq>‘Where are their mighty ones, The rock in whom they sought refuge?</dq>
[38] <dq>Who ate the fat of their slaughterings, And drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them arise and help you, Let it be a hiding-place for you!</dq>
[39] <dq>See now that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn>, And there is no <dn>Elohim</dn> besides <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> put to death and <dn>I</dn> make alive. <dn>I</dn> have wounded, and <dn>I</dn> heal. And from <dn>My</dn> hand no one delivers!</dq>
[40] <dq>For <dn>I</dn> lift <dn>My</dn> hand to the heavens, And shall say: As <dn>I</dn> live forever,</dq>
[41] <dq>If <dn>I</dn> have sharpened <dn>My</dn> flashing sword, And <dn>My</dn> hand takes hold on judgment, <dn>I</dn> shall return vengeance to <dn>My</dn> enemies, And repay those who hate <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[42] <dq><dn>I</dn> make <dn>My</dn> arrows drunk with blood, And <dn>My</dn> sword devours flesh, With the blood of the slain and the captives, From the long-haired enemy chiefs.’</dq>
[43] “O nations, acclaim <dn>His</dn> people! For <dn>He</dn> avenges the blood of <dn>His</dn> servants, And returns vengeance to <dn>His</dn> adversaries, And shall pardon <dn>His</dn> land, <dn>His</dn> people.”

readings.title: The Living Word
readings.subtitle: Torah as the Absolute Source of Life
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:44] Then Mosheh came, with Hoshĕa son of Nun, and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.
[45] And when Mosheh ended speaking all these words to all Yisra’ĕl,
[46] he said to them, “Set your heart on all the words with which I warn you today, so that you command <dn>את</dn> your children to guard to do <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah.
[47] “For it is not a worthless Word for you, because it is your life, and by this Word you prolong your days on the soil which you pass over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn to possess.”

readings.title: The Command to Ascend Mount Neḇo
readings.subtitle: Mosheh Prepares to be Gathered to His People
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 32:48] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh that same day, saying,
[49] <dq>“Go up this mountain of the Aḇarim, Mount Neḇo, which is in the land of Mo’aḇ, which is opposite Yeriḥo, and look at <dn>את</dn> the land of Kena‘an, which <dn>I</dn> give to the children of Yisra’ĕl as a possession,</dq>
[50] <dq>and die on the mountain which you ascend, and be gathered to your people, as Aharon your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,</dq>
[51] <dq>because you trespassed against <dn>Me</dn> in the midst of the children of Yisra’ĕl at the waters of Meriḇah Qaḏĕsh, in the Wilderness of Tsin, because you did not set <dn>Me</dn> apart in the midst of the children of Yisra’ĕl.</dq>
[52] <dq>“For you are to look at <dn>את</dn> the land before you, but not enter there, into the land which <dn>I</dn> am giving to the children of Yisra’ĕl.”</dq>

readings.title: The Infinite Singularity
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH from Everlasting to Everlasting
readings.text:
[Psalm 90:1] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have been our refuge In all generations.
[2] Before the mountains were born, Or <dn>You</dn> had brought forth the earth and the world, Even from everlasting to everlasting <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Ěl</dn>.
[3] <dn>You</dn> turn man back to dust, And say, <dq>“Return, O children of men.”</dq>
[4] For a thousand years in <dn>Your</dn> eyes Are like yesterday that has past, Or like a watch in the night.
[5] <dn>You</dn> have swept them away, They are as a sleep, Like grass that springs up in the morning.
[6] In the morning it flourishes and springs up, At evening it is cut down and withered.

readings.title: Numbering Our Days
readings.subtitle: The Reality of Divine Displeasure
readings.text:
[Psalm 90:7] For we have been consumed by <dn>Your</dn> displeasure, And by <dn>Your</dn> wrath we are alarmed.
[8] <dn>You</dn> have set our crookednesses before <dn>You</dn>, Our secret sin in the light of <dn>Your</dn> face.
[9] For all our days have passed away in <dn>Your</dn> wrath, We spend our years like a whisper.
[10] The days of our lives are seventy years; Or if due to strength, eighty years, Yet the best of them is but toil and exertion; For it is soon cut off, and we fly away.
[11] Who knows the power of <dn>Your</dn> displeasure? And <dn>your</dn> wrath, according to the fear of <dn>You</dn>?
[12] Teach us to number our days, And let us bring the heart to wisdom.

readings.title: The Petition for Restoration
readings.subtitle: Establishing the Work of Our Hands
readings.text:
[Psalm 90:13] Return, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! How long? And be sorry for <dn>Your</dn> servants.
[14] Satisfy us in the morning with <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment, And let us sing for joy all our days!
[15] Give us joy according to The days <dn>You</dn> have afflicted us, The years we have seen evil.
[16] Reveal <dn>Your</dn> work to <dn>Your</dn> servants, And <dn>Your</dn> splendour to their children.
[17] And let the pleasantness Of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> be upon us, And confirm the work of our hands for us; O confirm the work of our hands!
